public_rationale: Zitron says that because Microsoft keeps growing, 'things will stay the same.' He does not define 'things', and he gives no timeframe. In the next sentence he predicts that the system will collapse 'at some point'. A People Matters report of 5 August 2026, citing Business Insider, says Microsoft is retiring its Perspectives peer feedback tool. It says this is part of a wider overhaul of performance reviews that includes simplified rating categories (e1). That report does not show whether 'things' in Zitron's sense changed. It also says nothing on whether growth played any causal role. Without a defined outcome or period, the claim cannot be scored.
limitations: e1 is a single secondary report based on Business Insider's account of an internal message.
Treating particular review tools as decisive would add criteria Zitron did not supply.

statement.excerpt: Yet because the company keeps growing, things will stay the same.

our_interpretation: 'Things' seems to mean the workplace culture he criticizes: the growth-mindset framing, the Connect review process, and AI use in reviews. He does not define it.

The claim gives growth as the cause and offers no timeframe. In the next sentence he predicts the system will collapse 'at some point', so 'stay the same' is not a firm forecast with a measurable endpoint.
criteria.support_condition: Not adjudicable: the evidence needed would be a defined set of practices persisting over a defined period, plus proof that growth caused it. The speaker gives neither.
criteria.contradiction_condition: Not adjudicable for the same reason. Changes to particular review tools do not clearly show that 'things' changed in the sense he meant.
